title: Washboard and homemade bass clarinet with Blythe, O'Brien and Morton
summary: He took over washboard for Jasper Taylor with Jimmy Blythe and Jimmy O'Brien at Paramount, then built a bass-clarinet-like novelty horn that Jelly Roll Morton liked.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Great clarinet player. And then Jasper Taylor had produced the washboard on records at that particular time. And so Jasper's, and he went away on a big job. And Jimmy O'Brien, Jimmy Blythe was such close friends of mine, and he asked me if I would use this washboard in Jasper's place, because he knowed I was playing washboard as a novelty instrument all the time before Jasper started it. But I hadn't become popular like that.

So then I'd taken it up with Jimmy O'Brien and Jimmy Blythe. And so after we kept on with the Paramount people doing this, the novelty stuff, and so then I'd come in some fooling around, going around Jell-O'-Roll Morton, and I know each other well. So I'd come in and fooling around in with that kazoo part.

Then I made me a little invention I'd come up with. I bought a secondhand clarinet, tore it apart, and made it shaped like a bass clarinet. And I come in some playing this thing, so Jell-O'-Roll Morton fell for it. Yeah. He liked it simply because the fellow that was playing what you call a cone, just a plain cone.
